- [x] **I5** Sign and install IPAs with your own certificate, on the website (user 2026-11-17: 'do we have our own way to sign and load ipas using a mobile provision cert? we should'). Cydian's own signer, not another project's. Settings > Signing: the user picks their .p12, its password and a .mobileprovision; the page shows the certificate name, team, expiry and how many devices the profile lists, and keeps the files in IndexedDB on that phone only. On an AltStore app's page (F29), Install becomes Sign & Install when a certificate is set: the browser uploads the IPA URL plus the cert, profile and password to POST /sign over HTTPS; the server (web/app.py, a new web/signer/) downloads the IPA (size cap, http/https only, no private addresses: SSRF), signs it with zsign (check its licence fits GPL-3.0-or-later and record it; built into the Docker image) using the profile's entitlements and bundle ID, holds the signed IPA under a random unguessable token for 10 minutes, and answers with an itms-services:// link whose manifest and IPA it serves from that token; the page opens it. Privacy, stated on the page: the certificate, key and password are used in memory for that one request and never written to disk or logs; signed IPAs are deleted after 10 minutes or first download. Rate-limit per address. Clear errors for a wrong password, an expired cert or profile, or a profile whose app ID doesn't fit. - [x] **B64** (follow-up, critical) Sideload: other apps went through the server's /sign/host, which is only meant for iFizBox's own update (user 2026-11-18, 0.9.8: an update failed with 'server: This server hosts only iFizBox's own signed app' while signing with a * wildcard profile, so iFizBox's own ID was com.ryha.ifizbox and allowed: the refused upload was another app). Likely cause: Sideload.hostServer is one static var (native/Sources/Sideload.swift ~L137, set at L151 by each signing.install and L521 by each resign call, read at L306 after signing finishes on SignBridge.queue). When the queue starts the next job while the previous one is still signing (queue.js passes host only for iFizBox's own job, ~L427/L448, and 'after' lets jobs overlap), iFizBox's call sets hostServer and an app signed earlier then reads it and uploads to /sign/host. Fix: decide hosting per call (capture the host server in the job/closure; never a shared static), likewise manifestServer if it has the same problem; MyIPAs.swift L219 too. Other apps must always install from the phone's own 127.0.0.1 server (the host also caps uploads at 25 MB). The Worker now accepts any app on /sign/host (HOST_IDS '*', so the symptom is gone for small apps), but big apps would still fail there. Check: a test for the per-call host choice if the Swift side has a test path (else a JS-side test that only iFizBox's own job sends host: true, and the journal reasoning for the Swift change); native/build.sh builds both; tools/check.sh. When the certificate or profile can't do the new way well (development profile: sandbox push only; no Push / aps-environment production; a wildcard profile, which Apple won't give Push), say so before signing (it still keeps the ID if R25 says that installs; else falls back to your ID and says that) and link a help page: a new guide (screens/guides.js) with R25's steps made simple: make an explicit App ID with Push on, register your iPhones' UDIDs, make an Ad Hoc profile for it, import it in Settings > Signing. - [x] **B71a** Jailbreak build: queue AltStore apps from a row (swipe, hold menu) and from the app page's Modify, as tweaks queue: no install at once and no confirm popup on Remove (user 2026-11-19: 'it just adds to the queue'). Today app rows don't swipe in the jailbreak build (B71 checked on the iPhone 7: OpenTennis in Changes does nothing) because its only queue is apt's; the app queue (app-queue.js) signs, which the jailbreak build refuses. Needs: app jobs (Install/Upgrade/Remove) in a queue the jailbreak Confirm sheet and Q'd badge show, and a run that installs through the helper's install-ipa (ipa-install.js installWithAppSync) and removes through the Installed tab's helper uninstall (installed.js runDelete), quietly from a swipe with the undo bar (F193). Groundwork in browse.js: rowMenuItems({ jbApps, job, installed, newest }) and jailbreakAppRowState(item, { pkg, rec }) (tested in screens/rowswipe-jailbreak.test.js), not wired yet. The sideload (Lite) build's app-row swipe (F213 attachAppSwipe) must keep working: check it too. Check on the 7: swipe an app row in Changes and Search, Confirm runs it. | files: web/app/screens/browse.js, web/app/screens/queue.js, web/app/screens/apprun.js, web/app/core/appqueue.js, web/app/screens/*.test.js
- [x] **B92** Long IPA file names are cut off with no way to read them all (user 2026-11-19, Lite 0.9.9: opentennis-beta-p146.ipa ends in '…' and a tap doesn't show the rest). Do it the iOS 6 way: (1) file names truncate in the middle, so the start and the end stay visible ('opentennis-be…p146.ipa', like Mail attachments and Safari downloads; UILineBreakModeMiddleTruncation). CSS can't do that, so add one small JS helper that fits the name to the width, used by every row that shows an IPA or .deb file name (My IPAs, the install/progress page, the queue, Install IPAs). Keep tail truncation for app names and other text. (2) Hold a file-name row: the iOS 6 black Copy callout copies the full name, as Contacts does on a value row. If a tap opens the IPA's page, that page shows the full name wrapped, never cut. Check: node --test for the helper (short name unchanged; long name keeps the extension and the start; fits the given width), then a 3x render zoomed in on My IPAs with a long name, and tools/check.sh. | files: web/app/core/midtrunc.js, web/app/core/midtrunc.test.js, web/app/screens/myipas.js, web/app/myipas.css, web/app/progress.css, web/app/queue.css, web/app/screens/progress.js — concept approved
- [x] **B91** Lite: never open iOS's Install prompt again by itself. B89's freeze fallback (Sideload.swift hostAfterFreeze) uploads the IPA to /sign/host and then calls InstallPrompt.open(hosted…), so a new 'Install?' pops up unasked. The user may have tapped Cancel, and iFizBox can't tell a cancelled prompt from a frozen server. Keep the upload, but don't open the prompt: the row ends Cancelled, as B85's dismissed path does ('Cancelled on the iOS prompt'), and offers Install again. Only the user's tap (the row's re-prompt, signing.reprompt) opens the prompt, using the hosted link when the local listener froze, or else the local one. Look at InstallPrompt's own automatic re-opens (checkShown, and the B85 'retried when iOS drops it' path) too: re-opening when no prompt ever appeared is fine, re-opening after a prompt was shown and closed is not. Check: native tests pass with a test that a freeze after the prompt closed opens no new prompt; on the phone, Cancel on the prompt gives a Cancelled row with no new prompt, and Install again installs, also after the phone locked. | files: native/Sources/Sideload.swift, native/Sources/InstallPrompt.swift, native/test_install_server.py, web/app/core/apprun.js, web/app/screens/apprun.js — User 2026-11-19, replaces 'ends Cancelled': iFizBox can't tell the user's Cancel from a frozen server, so don't call it Cancelled. The row ends Failed with a generic line, for example 'iOS didn't download it', and the retry (Try Again) is open on that row. The tap opens the prompt again, as above (the hosted link when the listener froze). Keep 'Cancelled' only for what iFizBox knows: the user's own Stop or Cancel in iFizBox. Revisit B85's dismissed path ('Cancelled on the iOS prompt') to match: the same generic Failed with Try Again.

- [x] **B95** (follow-up, critical) Website Install of big IPAs breaks off: the Worker runs out of CPU. User 2026-11-19: Unbound (104 MB, github.com/marioparaschiv/unbound/releases/download/discord-354.0-ios/Unbound.ipa) failed with 'The app's download broke off before the end', several times. Reproduced with curl on ifizbox.com/api/fetch?kind=ipa: 6 of 8 downloads stopped short (175 KB to 99 MB of 104 MB) and ended cleanly instead of with an error. wrangler tail (-c wrangler.ifizbox.toml) shows outcome exceededCpu 'Worker exceeded CPU time limit' on every one. GitHub on its own sends the whole file in under 2 s. Cause: ipaFetch (worker/src/index.js) pipes the body through a JS TransformStream (the byte cap and B87's short-end check), so every chunk costs Worker CPU time. Fix: return r.body untouched (new Response(r.body, ...)), with no JS per chunk, so Cloudflare streams it natively and Content-Length survives. Keep the up-front Content-Length > max refusal. downloadIpa (web/app/signing-client.js) already checks the max and X-IPA-Length on the phone, so it still catches a short body; keep sending X-IPA-Length. Check: deploy, then run curl 10 times on the Unbound URL and get 104175897 bytes every time, with no exceededCpu in wrangler tail. If plain pass-through still goes over the CPU limit, add a resumed download: downloadIpa asks again with Range from byte n and the Worker passes Range through. If neither works, the website must say in words which apps are too big for it (the user wants a hard limit stated). Also fix the leftover home-screen icon: the early install link (F121) leaves a blank, stuck icon on the home screen when signing fails after iOS was sent to the link. Look at whether the failure can tell the Worker to answer iOS's held app.ipa with an error so iOS drops the icon, and otherwise tell the user in the failure text to delete the icon. | files: worker/src/index.js, worker/test.mjs, web/app/signing-client.js, web/app/download-cut.test.js — Also check the other leg, which My IPAs files (picked in Files, kept in IndexedDB) go through too: iOS reading app.ipa from /sign/up/<token>/app.ipa (worker/src/index.js, the ReadableStream pull loop). It copies each 20 MB KV part with data.slice in JS, about 5 copies for a 104 MB app, and could also hit exceededCpu. Test it: sign and upload a 100 MB IPA, curl app.ipa about 5 times, and watch wrangler tail. If it goes over, enqueue the part itself (a Uint8Array view, or KV's stream type) instead of a copy. - [x] **B93** Selecting text in the install log is very laggy while an install runs, and after Select All the Copy callout took a long time to show (user 2026-11-19, Lite 0.9.9, R19's install). Fix: batch log lines into one requestAnimationFrame append at most (never set innerHTML/textContent of the whole log), merge repeated progress lines into the line they update, and while a selection is inside the log (selectionchange) hold new lines in a buffer and append them once the selection ends. Keep it at 120 Hz: no layout reads in the append path. - [x] **B151** Local signing route (Lite): installing X (com.atebits.Tweetie2) failed with IXErrorDomain Code=46 'A coordinated app install already exists ... (creator App Store) but request by mobile_installation_proxy had scope requirement IXCoordinatorScopeRequirementRequired' (user 2026-11-20). The install had been slow, user switched away from the app and came back, then saw the raw APIInternalError dump plus '1 failed'. Cause: the App Store holds an install coordinator for that bundle ID (an App Store update/download in progress or stuck placeholder). Fix: (1) recognise IX Code 46 / 'coordinated app install already exists' in the error mapping (web/app/core/apprun.js) and show a plain message: the App Store is installing or updating this app; wait for it or cancel it from the Home Screen (long-press icon), then Retry. Never dump the raw error as the main line. (2) Check whether leaving the app mid-install makes our route hang or retry into this; if so handle the resume. Check: unit test in apprun.test.js with the user's error string gives the friendly line. | files: web/app/core/apprun.js, web/app/core/apprun.test.js, web/app/screens/apprun.js — user: the original App Store X was installed at the time, may be the cause (App Store-owned app with the same bundle ID; an auto-update or its coordinator). Check both causes. If it's the App Store copy, say so in the message too: delete the App Store X first, or install with Keep Bundle IDs off so it gets its own ID. — user update: deleting the App Store X did NOT help, same Code 46 right after. So a stale App Store coordinator for com.atebits.Tweetie2 outlives the app (e.g. a pending/stuck App Store update or the earlier slow attempt). Look for a way to clear or wait out the existing coordinator (installation_proxy/IX options, a retry after a delay), else the message says: restart the iPhone, then Retry. Screenshot: Apps/Log sheet with the raw error twice. — user update 2: a restart did NOT clear it either; the App Store coordinator for com.atebits.Tweetie2 persists across reboots (installcoordinationd keeps it, likely a pending App Store download/placeholder). So: (1) detect Code 46 and offer 'Install with its own bundle ID' (Keep Bundle IDs off for this app) as the one-tap way out, since a different ID has no coordinator; (2) find whether anything we can reach (installation_proxy, lockdown) lists or cancels the stale coordinator; the iPhone 15 read-only lockdown probe (memory: iphone15-lockdown-over-wifi) may help confirm, read only. — ROOT CAUSE (user 2026-11-20): not the App Store. The user had started X on BOTH routes, the Signing Server (OTA itms-services install, which iOS tags 'creator App Store') and the local route; the OTA install held the coordinator, so the local one got Code 46. X did install in the end. So the fix is: (1) Code 46 maps to one short line, e.g. 'X: already being installed by another install. Wait for it to finish.', with the raw error only in the Log; drop the App Store / restart / Keep Bundle IDs advice from the earlier notes; (2) don't start a second install of the same bundle ID while one is in flight on either route (skip it with that same line, or wait for the first).

Hint style rule (AGENTS.md via F311, concept https://claude.ai/artifact/JMn57UQTZkom6h1Uttz261): a footer explains only the group above it, one or two short sentences, split groups per switch, never joined footers, footer becomes the fix when something is off, status rows get none. - [x] **T53** Deploy ifizbox.com on release tags (v*) instead of every push to main. Today Cloudflare Workers Builds deploys on every push (worker/wrangler.ifizbox.toml, README.md:260, worker/README.md:104, docs/release.md). How: a GitHub Actions workflow on push tags 'v*' that runs tools/buildinfo.sh && cd worker && npx wrangler deploy -c wrangler.ifizbox.toml, using a CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN repo secret (+ account id). Watch out: tools/publish.sh tags in step 3 but commits web/app/source.json in step 4, after the tag, so a tag deploy would miss the new source: reorder so the deployed commit has it (or deploy from main at tag time), and keep publish.sh step 5's live check working. Update the docs to say deploys happen on tags. The owner must do two things by hand (list them clearly in the task's report, don't attempt): add the API token secret in GitHub, and turn off Workers Builds' auto-deploy on main in the Cloudflare dashboard. Check: workflow YAML is valid (actionlint if present), tools/check.sh passes, publish.sh --dry-run still runs. | files: .github/**, tools/publish.sh, tools/release.sh, worker/**, README.md, docs/release.md — Change of plan (owner): no GitHub Action and no repo secret. wrangler is already logged in on this machine (OAuth, workers_scripts:write), so tools/publish.sh deploys ifizbox.com itself right after it tags: tools/buildinfo.sh && cd worker && npx wrangler deploy -c wrangler.ifizbox.toml, from the tagged commit that already has the new source.json, before step 5's live check. Also a tools/deploy.sh (or publish.sh --deploy-only vX.Y.Z) to redeploy a tag by hand. The only manual step left: turn off Workers Builds' push deploy in the Cloudflare dashboard (wrangler's OAuth token gets 'Authentication error' on the Workers Builds API, checked 2026-11-20).

- [x] **F344** Know which app every tweak is for before anyone opens it, so Add Tweaks for an app lists only the tweaks that work in it (user 2026-11-21). Today the Lite filter reads only Packages fields (core/tweakfields.js injectableFromFields); the real target (the .deb's filter plist Filter.Bundles/Executables, core/tweaks.js inspectTweakDeb/filterBundles/targetsApp) is known only for packages already opened (screens/tweaks.js cachedTweakInfo, madeForRows), so hundreds of SpringBoard/system tweaks that can't work outside a jailbreak are offered. (1) A shared tweak index on ifizbox.com: the Worker (cron + on demand, worker/src, D1 or KV, env.FETCH, SSRF rules, size caps) downloads each free tweak .deb of the known/added Tweak Sources once per package+version, runs the same inspect (bundles, executables, anyApp, systemOnly, dylibs, needs) and serves GET /api/tweaks?source=…[&bundle=…]; the app and site read it, with the on-device inspect as the fallback for sources the index hasn't seen (background, capped, cached). (2) Lite: hide tweaks whose filter is SpringBoard/system-only (com.apple.springboard, backboardd, Preferences, daemons) or has no dylib; a tweak's row says 'Works in: YouTube' (appNameOf); Add Tweaks for an app shows tweaks that target that bundle ID first, then every-app (UIKit/Foundation) ones, nothing else. (3) Paid tweaks that can't be downloaded: list only when the source names a seller, with the target from Description/Name as a hint marked unverified. - [x] **F97** Cydian Account (user 2026-11-18: minimal, free to host): keep your settings, sources, ignored upgrades, installed-app records and signing certificate on cydian.dev, so a new phone, a reinstall or the website gets them back. No email, no password: the account is a random 128-bit **account key** made on the device (shown once as a code and a `cydian://account?k=` link / QR to save or open on another device; kept in the keychain in the app, IndexedDB on the site). Everything is encrypted on the device (AES-GCM, key from the account key with HKDF; Web Crypto in both builds), so cydian.dev only ever holds ciphertext and can't read a certificate. The Worker stores one blob per account in the existing KV namespace (`HOSTED`, a new `acct:` prefix; Cloudflare's free tier: 1 GB, 1,000 writes/day), keyed by SHA-256 of a separate HKDF-derived id, so the key never reaches the server: `PUT /api/account/<id>` (body ≤ 256 KB, an `If-Match` version so two devices don't overwrite each other: the second gets 409 and merges), `GET` (404 when none), `DELETE`. Rate-limit per address, refuse bodies over the cap, no logging of bodies. The payload is `websitePayload()`'s shape (screens/importlink.js: sources, settings, holds, identity) plus core/installed.js's records, versioned (`v: 1`). Settings > Account (iOS 6 grouped table): Create Account / Sign In With Key, Sync Now, Last Synced, Show Account Key, Delete Account (red, asks first); a Sync Certificate switch (on by default, with a footer saying it's encrypted with your key). Signing in is a read. Writes are batched (user 2026-11-18, the free tier's 1,000 writes/day): save once when the app goes to the background or the page is hidden, only if something changed since the last save, plus Sync Now; read on launch. Purchases stay with the repo's own account (Havoc, Chariz), not here. Last-write-wins per field with sources and holds merged as sets. Losing the key loses the data: say so when it's made. t: node tests for encrypt/decrypt round-trip, the id not revealing the key, merge rules and the 409 path against a fake backend; worker tests for the size cap, version check and delete. | files: web/app/core/account.js, web/app/screens/account.js, web/app/screens/settings.js, worker/src/**, native/Sources/** | test: web/app/core/account.test.js, worker tests — User 2026-11-18: approved as drafted. — F102 added a Wish List (localStorage cydian.wishlist, core/wishlist.js): sync it beside holds.

- [x] **F97** Cydian Account (user 2026-11-18: minimal, free to host): keep your settings, sources, ignored upgrades, installed-app records and signing certificate on cydian.dev, so a new phone, a reinstall or the website gets them back. No email, no password: the account is a random 128-bit **account key** made on the device (shown once as a code and a `cydian://account?k=` link / QR to save or open on another device; kept in the keychain in the app, IndexedDB on the site). Everything is encrypted on the device (AES-GCM, key from the account key with HKDF; Web Crypto in both builds), so cydian.dev only ever holds ciphertext and can't read a certificate. The Worker stores one blob per account in the existing KV namespace (`HOSTED`, a new `acct:` prefix; Cloudflare's free tier: 1 GB, 1,000 writes/day), keyed by SHA-256 of a separate HKDF-derived id, so the key never reaches the server: `PUT /api/account/<id>` (body ≤ 256 KB, an `If-Match` version so two devices don't overwrite each other: the second gets 409 and merges), `GET` (404 when none), `DELETE`. Rate-limit per address, refuse bodies over the cap, no logging of bodies. The payload is `websitePayload()`'s shape (screens/importlink.js: sources, settings, holds, identity) plus core/installed.js's records, versioned (`v: 1`). Settings > Account (iOS 6 grouped table): Create Account / Sign In With Key, Sync Now, Last Synced, Show Account Key, Delete Account (red, asks first); a Sync Certificate switch (on by default, with a footer saying it's encrypted with your key). Signing in is a read. Writes are batched (user 2026-11-18, the free tier's 1,000 writes/day): save once when the app goes to the background or the page is hidden, only if something changed since the last save, plus Sync Now; read on launch. Purchases stay with the repo's own account (Havoc, Chariz), not here. Last-write-wins per field with sources and holds merged as sets. Losing the key loses the data: say so when it's made. t: node tests for encrypt/decrypt round-trip, the id not revealing the key, merge rules and the 409 path against a fake backend; worker tests for the size cap, version check and delete. | files: web/app/core/account.js, web/app/screens/account.js, web/app/screens/settings.js, worker/src/**, native/Sources/** | test: web/app/core/account.test.js, worker tests — User 2026-11-18: approved as drafted. — F102 added a Wish List (localStorage cydian.wishlist, core/wishlist.js): sync it beside holds.

Cause: tools/release.sh runs tools/selfrepo.py over only that release's .debs, and each stanza's Filename: is a bare asset name that the Worker's /repo/<file> fetches from releases/latest/download/, so older .debs aren't reachable either. Fix: Packages keeps a stanza per published release (read the earlier releases' Debian-named .debs or their Packages asset; cap like altsource.py's 20), each Filename: a path the Worker maps to that release's asset (e.g. /repo/<tag>/<file> -> releases/download/<tag>/<file>, same SSRF/size rules, no redirect for Zebra), and docs/release.md says so. Check: test_selfrepo.py with two releases, apt on the iPhone 7 sees both versions (apt-cache policy com.ryha.ifizbox), iFizBox's Modify > Downgrade lists them. | files: tools/selfrepo.py, tools/release.sh, tools/test_selfrepo.py, worker/src/**, docs/release.md

- [x] **B84** (follow-up, normal) In the jailbreak app, installing iFizBox's own .deb from inside iFizBox (seen with Modify > Downgrade to 0.9.8-1557 on the iPhone 7; the Upgrade banner / Changes upgrade of com.ryha.ifizbox very likely goes the same way) leaves dpkg with com.ryha.ifizbox 'half-configured': apt's term.log for that run never ends, and every later apt-get (iFizBox's own installs included) stops with 'dpkg was interrupted, you must manually run dpkg --configure -a'. Likely cause: the helper's apt-get runs as a child of the app, and postinst's 'uicache -p' on the running app makes iOS close the app, which takes apt, dpkg and postinst down with it. Fix ideas: run a self-install's apt detached from the app (setsid/launchd job, or the upgrades daemon), or skip/defer uicache when the app is the caller, and have the helper run 'dpkg --configure -a' when it finds an interrupted dpkg. Check on the 7 afterwards: dpkg -s com.ryha.ifizbox shows 'install ok installed' after an in-app downgrade and upgrade. Details: journal/2026-11-19-r28-downgrade-older-builds. | files: native/helper/**, native/deb/postinst, native/Sources/Apt.swift
- [x] **B88** (follow-up, low) Jailbreak queue run (F234, one package at a time) with iFizBox's own package (com.ryha.ifizbox) and others: nothing orders iFizBox last, so once its dpkg run puts the new Info.plist on disk the app's Replaced watcher (App.swift, 3 s timer) closes the app and the packages queued after it never run (likely; not tried on the phone; found in B84, which made the apt run itself survive the app closing). Fix idea: core/installrun.js puts iFizBox's own row last in the dpkg lane (after everything that doesn't depend on it), and/or Replaced holds its close while a helper run is going. Check on the 7: queue iFizBox + a small package, both install. | files: web/app/core/installrun.js, web/app/core/installrun.test.js
- [x] **F253** (follow-up, low) UDID from a configuration profile on the website: the Worker serves a Profile Service .mobileconfig (PayloadType Profile Service, DeviceAttributes UDID/PRODUCT/VERSION, a per-visit Challenge, URL = an https /udid endpoint); iOS POSTs a CMS-signed plist, the Worker reads the plist out of it (find <?xml ... </plist>, no crypto), keeps {udid, product, version} in KV under the challenge for the TTL, and answers 301 to a page that says to go back. The website (Safari or the Home Screen web app, which don't share storage, so it polls the Worker by challenge) then fills This iPhone in Settings > Signing, which today says unknown for any profile with a device list. Unsigned profile shows Not Verified: say so on the page. Background: journal/2026-11-19-r30-free-apple-id/notes.md section 4. | files: worker/src/udid.js, worker/src/index.js, worker/test.mjs, web/app/screens/signing.js, web/app/screens/settings.js, docs/signing.md

- [x] **B96** (follow-up, low) Range reads of /sign/up/<token>/app.ipa cost ~37 ms Worker CPU (seen in wrangler tail, 2026-11-19): a Range's cut first/last part is read whole as arrayBuffer (20 MB each) in upPump. Read only what's needed (KV stream, skip natively or cancel early) so iOS's Range requests stay under the CPU limit. | files: worker/src/index.js, worker/test.mjs
